title: Large coproducts descend from the derived category
statement: Let A be a locally w-small Grothendieck abelian category with a chosen w-Hom derived category. If D(A) has coproducts indexed by types in universe max(w,vA,vH), where vA is the Hom universe of A, then A has coproducts indexed at the same size. No preservation assertion for arbitrary derived coproducts is made.

source.place: Original proof step 1: agent-written derived-to-abelian coproduct transfer, extending Stacks Project Tag 0F5S

proof.text: For the family X_j, form K=∐_j X_j[0] in the derived category and P=H⁰(K). Define injections X_j -> P by the inverse single-object homology isomorphism followed by H⁰ of the derived injection. The injective homology comparison, its compatibility with composition, and the derived coproduct universal property prove bijectivity of Hom_A(P,I) -> product_j Hom_A(X_j,I) for injective I.

For arbitrary Y, embed it into Injective.under Y. Extend the family of maps X_j -> Y to a unique map a:P -> Injective.under Y. Postcompose with the cokernel and its monomorphism into an injective. Bijectivity on this second injective proves the composite is zero. Cancel the monomorphism, and use Abelian.monoLift to factor a through Y. Cancel the first monomorphism to verify the coprojection equations and uniqueness. Package these maps as a colimiting cofan and transport to the original discrete diagram.
